title: Wet side, dry side
text: The Santa Lucia Range, the mountains around Adelaida, catches the Pacific's moisture on its western slopes and leaves the valley to its east, where Paso Robles lies, much drier. Here on the drier east side, the slopes carry chaparral and open woods of pine and oak, while the ocean side of the range grows redwoods and Douglas fir. At the Paso Robles airport, only about 12 inches of rain falls in an average year. In the Adelaida wine district, up on the range's slopes, it is about 25 inches.

s1.title: Santa Lucia Range
s1.quote: the mountains' close proximity to the Pacific Ocean causes moisture to be deposited on the west-facing slopes, creating a suitable environment for conifers. This creates a rain shadow over the Salinas Valley to the east, which is considerably drier. ... The western slopes of the range facing the Pacific Ocean are moist with growths of coast redwood, Douglas fir ... The east side is drier, with chaparral and open woods of pine (including Coulter pine and gray pine) and oak woodlands of several Quercus species.

s2.title: Paso Robles, California
s2.quote: The city lies along the Salinas River on California's Central Coast.
